utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-81-T, The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier and Barney Thomas for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and to all. Boris Zorko, Chad Mair, Alex Fielding, and Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Good afternoon, Mr. Kodzopeljic. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to remind you, Mr. Kodzopeljic, I know you know this already, but it is still our duty to remind you that you're still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can have but a moment. We seem to be have a technical problem still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We still have a minor technical problem. We're going to try to work around it. But in the event that we have to go to the ELMO, we are not in a position to see both the transcript of the proceedings as well as whatever exhibit is being shown to the witness. And to the extent there are any issues, it can be addressed to me specifically by Mr. Zorko as they relate to translations, that puts out as somewhat of a disadvantage for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Join the club, Mr. Guy-Smith. We also can't see anything on our screens. I'm being advised that we should use the other one that is the one over which have you no control for LiveNote. And then within five minutes the other one will work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to continue where we left off yesterday. I -- I note that you have your binder in front of you, and I'd like you to take a look at the next document which is P589.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going suggest that we do, for the purposes of -- of the examination at this point, is I'm going to ask you a series about the document which you have in hard copy, and then we can either have it on the screen -- have the document on the screen as we normally would, but then we would not have the benefit of the transcript, or we can just work for a minute with the document. You know what? Let me make another suggestion. Let me try to do something somewhat different for the moment, because if it's going to be five minutes, perhaps what I can do is jump into -- I can go to another subject matter for a moment, and I come back to this subject and see if we can do it that way. That might be probably a more efficacious use of our time. Mr. Kodzopeljic, during the period of -- of our discussions over the last couple of days we have, in large measure, been discussing the issue of special-purpose industry, and we have touched upon your specific duties in the technical administration. What I'd like you to do, if you could, is I'd like you to explain to us the technical institutes and how the military technical institutes, and specifically the military institutes with regard to repair, fit into your duties, if you could.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak of the technical and maintenance institutes that were under me. It was the institute in Kragujevac [Realtime transcript read in error "Kraljevic"] and Cacak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to those institutes, what were -- what was the institute in Cacak responsible for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute in Cacak maintained non-combat [as interpreted] motor vehicles, tanks, APCs, infantry weapons, in the sense of general maintenance. Next, they also maintained some engineering and electronic equipment, as well as internal combustion engines, and that was the bulk of their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the institute in Kraljevic [sic]. Could you -- could you describe for us what its -- it did?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical and maintenance depot or institute in Kragujevac [Realtime transcript read in error "Kraljevic"] was specific, because it only maintained and worked on ammunitions. As far as I can tell you, based on the principles of economics, they worked on ammunitions of the -- of the 20 millimetre calibre onwards or upwards. It simply was not cost effective to maintain any ammunitions below that range. I can also tell you that they worked on other types of mines and explosives, but for the most part, they worked with the ordnance that was of 20 millimetre calibre and up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask -- okay. Just before I do that, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I think there's an error in the transcript. The institute that was referred to, at least what I heard Mr. Kodzopeljic refer to, was Kragujevac, and it's been recorded as "Kraljevic," page 3, line 25, and page 4, line 7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you please correct us, Mr. Kodzopeljic. Which was the correct name?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And line 9 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the technical and maintenance institute in Kragujevac, and the one before that is in Cacak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay just before the screen disappears --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The very line that is disappearing says: "The institute in Cacak maintained non-combat motor vehicles, tanks, APCs, infantry weapons." What do you mean by that? How can tanks and infantry weapons and APCs be non-combat vehicles? Unless you were misquoted, you were misinterpreted, but that's what the thing says here and now it's disappeared. I can't refer you to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then it must have been misinterpreted. I said that the technical institute in Cacak maintained those; whereas, the one in Kragujevac, maintained only on ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think that the Judge's question is slightly different than what you responded to, Mr. Kodzopeljic. You mentioned two kinds ever vehicles and hopefully we will get it back after the whole technical -- the whole LiveNote issue is taken care of. I don't want to take what he said out of context. So apparently my experiment to get into an area where we were not dealing with exhibits was not successful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that Mr. Guy-Smith. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And let me see if -- if we can work with your -- with your last answer by memory. You indicated that in Kragujevac there were two kinds of vehicles that were being maintained, and could you tell us again what those two kinds were?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There seems to be a misunderstanding. The technical maintenance institute in Kragujevac generally refitted ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies. That one I made a terrible mistake and I do apologise. Cacak.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The technical maintenance institute in Cacak maintained infantry weapons, armoured combat vehicles such as tanks, electronic equipment, vehicles, and I said non-combat motor vehicles, under which our -- the vehicles, the weight of which is .75 tons, 1, and 1 and a half tons. These are transport vehicles that are not fitted with weapons, and we referred to them as non-combat motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the important thing is that combat vehicles are also repaired there, APCs, and infantry weapons and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, you may proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, in the first institute that we discussed, Cacak, were vehicles built at that institute?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did not produce vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was their function limited to -- put it another way. What was their function limited to? It wasn't production. So what was done with these vehicles, be they combat or non-combat vehicles?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief. When a piece of equipment, combat or non-combat or whatever they had within their overhaul programme, is assessed as no longer be sufficient -- being sufficiently reliable to be used, it is sent to the technical and maintenance or overhaul institute in Cacak. Let's say it's a tank. They -- they then take it apart, control each and every part in terms of material, quality, and dimension, and then reassemble the tank. Should a part be of such poor quality that it could no longer be used, it is replaced by a new or repaired spare part. After that, the tank is tested and, if it passes the test, it is considered to be basically a new tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as a new -- as a new tank, once it -- it passes its test, does that tank then re-enter into the materiel of the VJ? Or is it used for some other -- or can it be used for some other purpose, or both?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It cannot be used for any other purpose. It remains a military asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the institute at Kragujevac, what was that institute responsible for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To repeat, that technical and overhaul institute was in charge of refitting ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you describe which -- to us what you mean by "refitting ammunition"?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, briefly. The technical characteristics of different types of ammunition is monitored, those stored in warehouses and generally used across the army, and based on the results of such monitoring, such types of ammunition that are found unsatisfactory are being refitted. Let's say it's a bullet. It is transported to the institute, disassembled. Each part is controlled to see whether it meets the technical characteristic threshold. It is cleaned. We technically refer to it as de-labouration. Following the exercise, the bullet is reassembled, and those parts that are found unfit are replaced, because they were not within the permissible range. After that, such a bullet is protected, packaged, and used as a new bullet for the next 15 or 20 years, depending on the type, the type of ammunitions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You talked here about bullets and indicated that they get packaged and used as new bullets for the next 15 or 20 years, depending on the type, the type of ammunitions. But with regard to mines, do mines have the same -- what I would call, and I don't know if this is a proper military term, but do mines have the same shelf-life that bullets have, or is their shelf-life different?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, it's the same. I can expand perhaps. The basic components used to determine shelf-life is the gunpowder and explosive material. We have a separate centre, an institution used to monitor the production of ammunitions. When any type of ammunition is produced, parts of explosive material are exempt and deposited in such monitoring centres. Each batch, each series is monitored for end date, and that is why I cannot tell you precisely what the shelf-life is for each and every type of ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have the distinct impression that you're starting to speed up in the delivery of your answers. If you could slow down a bit, I think it would be helpful to all. And I do apologise for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try. The shelf-life, after a general refitting process, depends on the shelf-life or degree of reliability and stability of such components built in during that process. In case of new ammunition, such materials are also monitored for their shelf-life.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to double-check something. On line 6, your answer reads the shelf-life after a generally fitting process?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: General refitting process.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you use the term "refitting," do you use that term in a -- in a fashion that synonymous with the term "repair." Is that the same term that you're using, they have the same meaning for you with regard the type of activity that's occurring?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the same type of activity. Repair is simply removing a single malfunction or two or three of them in a vehicle, for example. However, general refitting or a overhaul includes activities precisely prescribed by technological processes. They encompass a larger scope or a type of work that needs to be included in that process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying refitting means overhauling? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That would be what we refer to as general overhaul.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: In cases of "vehicles," we believe the more appropriate term would be "overhaul." In case of "ammunition," "refitting" seems to be the better term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With that in mind, I'd like, if you could, to explain in a brief manner the subject of reserves. And if you could tell us whether or not there's one system of reserves or multiple systems of reserves, to your knowledge, within VJ were there at the time that you were engaged in your work in the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a very broad area pertaining to the army as a whole. Globally speaking, reserves are categorised as wartime reserves and peacetime reserves or stocks. Wartime reserves are found at troop level, army level, and at the level of the Supreme Command. Peacetime stocks are usually found at the level of the Supreme Command and, to a certain extent, at the middle level.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's stop right there and discuss the issue of wartime reserves which you have told us are found at -- from what I can tell, three different areas. And by that I mean, troop level, army level, and the level of Supreme Commander. With regard to the troop level of reserves, wartime reserves that is, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything used in a war needs to be stockpiled in case there is a war and resupplied in times of war. Those are such reserves that a particular unit carries with it, enabling it to engage in combat activities according to a pre-planned or envisaged number of days of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the wartime reserves that existed at a troop level, can you tell us what happens when those reserves are exhausted, or is that something that does happen?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand your question well, if a unit is implementing certain tasks, be it in times of peace or war, it consumes. It uses a certain level of assets. The resupply needs to come from a higher level so as to enable the unit to continue pursuing those activities in peacetime and in wartime for a certain number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the resupply or replenishment to the troop level, where does that come from?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it this way. Every army has a hierarchical system of provisions. In other words there are several levels in providing various materials. For instance, if a unit expends a certain amount of some materiel, that will be resupplied by its subordinate [as interpreted] command and, for the most part, this is done from the army stockpiles, army reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On line 14, I'm looking at the answer, it says: "If a unit expends a certain amount of some materiel, that will be resupplied by its subordinate command." And that's a bit confusing to me. Would that be accurate, and I'm wondering if I have a translation --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It should be "superior command."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So for the troop, the next level up, would be what -- what would that be called? Would that be the army? Would it go directly from the troop to the army in terms of superior command?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depends. For instance, if we are a brigade its superior command would be a corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And as we go up the chain, as it were, in terms of reserves, do each one of these sections have their own reserves designated as belonging -- or designating as being to their benefit?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Each level of command has their own designated amount of reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now with regard to the issue of the reserves of the Supreme Command, are those reserves, the reserves of the Supreme Command, reserves that are utilised in the pipeline of replenishment to the troops in the -- in wartime?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what their purpose is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the wartime reserves of the Supreme Command, are those wartime reserves held collectively with all the others; or is there some way that the reserves are designated as belonging to, for example, the Supreme Command, as opposed to any army, corps, or brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would depend on the type of asset. A large part of the wartime reserves of the army and the Supreme Command are stockpiled in the same depots. But if you remember what we said about the material lists, they are completely separate. So they are held in the same depots but for record purposes, they are separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say they -- when you say that for record purposes they are separate, just so we have some understanding here, are the -- are they also physically kept separate from the other reserves? And by this I mean, do you have, for example, a designation that says, reserves Supreme Command; reserves 1st Army; reserves, corps; reserves, brigade. So you have actually in the area they are separated physically or is it a paper separation?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, our army was large and we had ammunition depots with a large number of warehouses. For instance, one depot sometimes had 30 -- up to 36 warehouses. And those warehouses were specifically designated and the handlers of those warehouses were different. Some handlers handled the army reserves whereas others handled the reserves of the command -- the Supreme Command. Because it didn't make financial sense, it wasn't efficient to hold the same assets in several different physical warehouses or areas because those facilities had to be protected from blasts. They had to be especially built. The power supply had to be in the so-called S-system, and there are many other specifications and rules and requirements to stockpile those reserves in a Safe way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You introduced here a concept which is a power supply that had to be in the so-called S-system. Could you describe for us, obviously in general terms, was the S-system is so that we understand the importance of it and why there had to be a power supply that had a particular kind of power or particular kind of electric -- electric format?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I just mentioned the power supply but the stockpiling or keeping reserves of ammunition and, of course, that would be different for tanks and cannons which are also stored in warehouses. But the regulations are very strict and very detailed. So, for instance, you're not allowed to use a certain type of shoe that can cause a certain electric short circuit or -- and the electric power system, the S-system is such that it makes it impossible for -- which makes it impossible for a short circuit to occur anywhere within that system. That would be roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. That's understood. With regard to the reserves that existed in the system of those reserves for purposes of the designation war reserves, have you covered the -- not the entirety in terms of every detail, but have you -- you've covered the basic system as it relates to war reserves. Because if we -- I'm going move on to peacetime reserves in a moment, but I want to make sure that we have fully ventilated this particular area of reserves.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In brief, that is a very complex system, and very responsible, in terms of security and its significance for the state.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now with regard to the -- the issue of use and replenishment, I take it that the -- at the end of every fiscal year, calendar year, or planning year, when you were talking about planning the budget for the next year, if it was the next -- for the next annual year or for the next five years, since you discussed both kinds of plans, the use of materiel and ultimately of the amount of materiel that was left was something of considerable importance to your planning?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. The quantities were very important. I have to say that every tactical handler, if you recall when we discussed this, had to take care and be aware of the quantities of his reserves. In other words, the technical service is not in charge of the quantities that will be stored, but, rather, the handler himself is responsible to plan the expenditure of those assets in the course of the dynamics of the work that is done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now with regard to the issue of peacetime reserves, was the system of peacetime reserves, storage and use, distinct from that of war reserves?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my service itself, the system was the same within our service. Ammunition of any type, whether it was wartime reserve or peacetime reserve, for me, in terms of its safekeeping, it -- it was absolutely identical. The system was identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I -- I want to go back here, because perhaps we have a translation issue; perhaps not. With regard to the -- the matter that you were discussing just a moment ago, that being the importance of having accurate understanding of this information for your planning, your answer states at line 23: "In other words, the technical service is not in charge of quantities that will be stored, but, rather, the handler himself is responsible to plan the expenditure of those" quantities, as I'm assuming the word that's missing, "in the course of the dynamic of the work that is done." And my question to you is: Is it the handler who is responsible plan the expenditure of those quantities?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I did not say that it was a handler. I -- rather, I said that this was determined by the level -- the tactical level. In other words, those who are responsible to implement it at their -- at the tactical level. If you'd like me to explain it in more detail, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Please do so, because I want to make sure that we know who is responsible for the job that is being performed.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we discussed the General Staff for instance in the land army of the General Staff. The land armies consisted of several administrations: The infantry administration, the armoured mechanised administration, the artillery administration, engineering administration, the chemical and biological weapons administration, and perhaps I didn't number them all, but if now we look at one of these administration, for instance the infantry administration, it is responsible, it is the holder. It is the subject and the planner and it will use all the infantry ammunition and weapons and it will take care and be responsible for replenishment of the reserves and their expenditures. If we're talking about the armoured administration, that administration would be responsible for handling and utilisation of the armoured vehicles to take care of the replenishment of ammunition for the armoured assets and the same is true for the engineering administration. Or me, for instance, I was in charge - in the logistics sector - I was in charge of electrical energy and the assets used therefore, and also for equipment, tools, workshops, and maintenance and repairs for all the assets that are used with an army unit. I think this would be it in brief. In other words let me repeat. These subjects were responsible for the quantities of reserves, their expenditures, their issuance and utilisation; whereas, the technical service was in charge of securing and stockpiling those and issuing them at the time when it is so required.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ordered by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again just to double-check something here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your last answer you said at line 23, "whereas the technical service was in charge of securing and stockpiling those and issuing them at the time whens it is so required. Is that technical service or is that technical something else? Is the term "technical service" the appropriate term to be using right there?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Generally speaking the technical service or, rather, the units and institutions within the technical service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You also said starting from line 19 on the other screen: "These subjects were responsible for the quantities of reserves, their expenditure, their issuance, and utilisation; whereas, the technical service ..." What do you call -- what was the official name of these subjects? Earlier you used the word "handler." I don't know whether those are the handlers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can only repeat one more time: We're not talking here about handlers but, rather, about agents or subjects at the tactical level such as, for instance, the infantry administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but what do you mean by subject? These are people, I suppose, and what -- what -- is that the official name? They are called subjects?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The administration -- the infantry administration, which, under the regulations, is responsible for that specific area. They are responsible for certain tasks, for instance. Those would be the subjects. We called them the tactical subjects or agents. Implementers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. So some are tactical; others are technical. Those who looked after stockpiling are called technical.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Support, technical support, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the issue of peacetime reserves, you indicated that they were -- for your purposes, your work was essentially the same. With regard to the issue of accounting and the need to have accurate records for purposes of planning, as regards a peacetime army, once again, would accurate records be of importance to you, in terms of being able to plan for the future, be it an annual or a five-year plan?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I've said that a number of times. For a tactical level subject, or agent, it is very important to know exactly what quantities of assets there are in -- in the whole system of warehouses. Maybe you didn't hear me. It is very important for every tactical level subject to know exactly how much of what there is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Irrespective of whether or not we're dealing with the issue of being a peacetime army, wartime army, or an army that's in flux, as a bottom line, which you've said here, which is: "It is very important for every tactical level subject to know exactly how much of what there is available."

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. I can confirm what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in the absence of -- in the absence for your purposes -- for your job of knowing what was available, what difficulties did it create for you, if any?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for us, it was important in terms of providing technical support, building and reconstructing warehouses, collecting certain types of materials in order to be more efficient. And I can tell you for instance that each facility that had stockpiles of rifles or pistols or similar weapons, they had to be especially fitted with special methods of stockpiling them, in order to prevent possible burglaries. For us, it was important to have this at our disposal, in the economic sense, the stockpiles that are available for the tactical level users, or subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to what you've just said, is that the -- is that the only importance that existed, or were there other reasons why it was important for you to know what was available?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't -- nothing else really comes to mind as to what kind of other problems there might be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Hopefully there were no other problems. I believe that the system is working again. And if such be the case, then I would like us to turn to P589.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine, except we have three minutes to dispose of before we take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Why don't we take a break now then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I can try. Let me try.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could turn to your binder to P589.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this particular document, I'd like you to take a look at -- as we have done before, the upper left-hand corner. I note that in box number 4, there is the name and the address of a sender. Do you see that? I'm sorry, there is information contained in box number 4 concerning the name and address of a sender. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is TRZ, Kragujevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to now go to the right-hand side of the document, the upper right-hand side of the document. I note that no information is contained in any of the boxes except for box number 14. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard do box number 14, could you tell what it says, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30th -- or 30.KC.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And do you know what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that stands for personnel centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this issue which is an issue that we discussed yesterday, is this an address where logistics could be sent, the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that. I cannot say that with certainty. But, as far as I knew, the 30th KC, that administration was in Belgrade down-town Belgrade. So it didn't make sense, for instance, for someone from Kragujevac to send ammunition to Belgrade. I believe that this has to do with something else. There's something -- something else going on here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. And after the break, we'll pick up ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We will take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In your last answer before the break, you said: "There's something else going on here." Do you recall making that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that it only says the 30th KC, and I can't say what could be behind that. I only know of the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just for a moment, with regard to the 30th Personnel Centre, do you know whether or not the 30th Personnel Centre was a name or designation for some specific institution other than that which is named here?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have much knowledge about the 30th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Continuing looking at the document, if we could, and directing your attention to box 24, a box that we have discussed before. Can you confirm that there is no nomenclature of either 12 or 13 digits in that box?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only the first four digits are there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we can scroll down to the bottom of the document, left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you see that there's -- both signatures as well as a stamp in boxes 32, 37, and 38?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the right hand -- bottom portion of the document, sir. If we could scroll to the right. With regard to the right hand portion of the document, would you agree that there is no signature in boxes 39 [sic], 40, 41?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aren't you referring to boxes 40, 41, and 42?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I am. And if I misspoke, your correction is appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because that concerns receipt. There is no signature there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And can you confirm there's no stamp?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is none.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Between 1993 and 1996, I wonder if you can help us with regard to an issue concerning your knowledge of whether or not there was any war profiteering that occurred concerning assets of the -- of your -- of the depots that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the -- the general issue of -- of war profiteering, was that a matter that was of concern to the technical administration at any level?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical administration did not deal with that. However, we were concerned, if such information reached us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And do you recall any such information reaching you?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall any. It was a long time ago. I presume I would need to be more specific, but I cannot recall anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could see P592.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now for P592, directing your attention to the upper left-hand corner, would you confirm that in the -- those boxes that we have been having discussions about, the only information that's contained in the upper left-hand corner is the box at number 4, where it says VJ?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that. And at the top of the page, it says "receipt."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You say at the top of the page it says "receipt." Are you referring to the -- to the -- the typed-in word which looks to me like "P-r-i-j-e-m"?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That word means "receipt"?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, receipt. It means it was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Before we go any further, I would note for the record that the translation is "delivery," not "receipt." In the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So this, unlike the matters that we referred to before, which were not subject to translation errors but, rather, insertions, into the document, this would seem to be a translation issue. I'm waiting for my -- my colleague to make a determination, although he seems to be have having some further inquiry, so I will continue on and we will get back to it today. Now, if we could go to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Thomas is standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, my mic is not working, Your Honours. Thank you. The difficulty for me, Your Honours, is, obviously, I can't tell what the appropriate translation of the word is. We just have to leave that for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very well. That's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could go to the lower left-hand side of the document, which will be on -- the next page in -- in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you see any entries in -- in the left-hand side of the document in boxes number 32, 37, 38, 39?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything. I only note the stamp over box 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us looking at that stamp where's that stamp from, if you can tell? Where does it signify it's from would be a better way of putting it.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp reads: Military Post 7111, Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind us, in which former republic of the SFRY is Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the upper right-hand side of the document, can we take a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And focussing your attention on box number 14, could you tell us what it says?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Drina Corps Command."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the informations contained in box 24, there are a number of different entries. Can you confirm for us that there is no nomenclature of either a 12- or 13-digit nature.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And finally looking at the lower right-hand side of this particular document. I note that there is in boxes number 40 and 41 typewritten what seems to be signatures. And that would be on the -- there you go. The second page of the English. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you do us another kindness and remind us --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems so to me, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, we didn't hear the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It seems so to me too. The missing answer, witness answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you do us the kindness of going back to the information that's contained in box number 4 where it says "VJ" and tell us what, if any, information that gives you with regard to the delivery of material?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the usual short form for Yugoslav Army, VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to it designating the name and place of sender for purposes of tracking where information came from, of what assistance is this information to you?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not of much help.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this has to do with the Army of Yugoslavia, then you know very well what size of territory it encompassed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that, I -- I take it that you -- I do know that it was a large territory. But can you be more specific in your comments as to why this is a difficulty, or why it is of little or no help?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I understand the thrust of your question better. It means that if these quantities were, indeed, supplied, no identification can be made in terms of what tactical agent saw their tactical reserves reduced. I cannot say whose reserves this came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we now see P595.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Referring your attention to the upper left-hand corner and specifically referring your attention to box number 4, is the information that's contained in box number 4 an address?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says NGS - VJ POV.BR,.85 - 89 of 22.09.95.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is that an address?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The reference is to an order or a document, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, that is the only part of the form that's filled out in the upper left-hand corner, and by that I am referring to the boxes 1 through 10. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I want to move in to the right-hand side of the document, going to box 14. In the previous exhibit that we saw, there was a stamp, and I believe that you indicated that -- that the stamp contained the same information that's contained in -- in box 14, and by that I mean Military Post 7111, Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only says H. Pijesak, as opposed to the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You are absolutely correct. And with regard to this military post, do you know apart from this military post being in the former -- at one point in the former SFRY and in Bosnia-Herzegovina, do you know where this -- where this military post was physically?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have any idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Guy-Smith, your question was -- in the previous exhibit that we saw there was a stamp, and I believe that you indicated that that stamp contained the name -- information that's contained in box 14, and by that I mean military post. I'm not quite sure, are you suggesting that that stamp was in box 14 or are you suggesting that what we saw on that stamp is the information that is now in box 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You -- you -- you have put it precisely with regard to the second part. And I wasn't trying to be confusing. I was talking about the information itself. Not the stamp, but the information itself that is contained on the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could direct our attention to box 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, in terms of the issue surrounding nomenclature, would you confirm that there is no nomenclature with regard to any of the six types of supplies that are listed?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could go down -- excuse me, if we could scroll -- thank you very much. Before we get to the bottom of the -- the form, after box number 6, there's some writing. Could you tell us what that says. It's a handwritten -- it's handwriting without a number in front of it. Can you tell us what that says?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the box number 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Directly below box number 6. In terms -- after the -- where you look at the type of supplies, there's six supplies listed. You go to the centre of the document. You're --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There's something --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says concluded with the ordinal number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After that, do you see anything further in that particular area of the document, the centre of the document. Is there any other handwritten information or -- or typewritten information?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I would note for the record that in the English document the following is inserted: "/illegible/ NGS-VJ/? Chief of General Staff," which is initial caps "- initial caps, Yugoslav Army /85-89, dated on 22.09.95." This insertion is not contained on the original document, which has been introduced as plaintiff's 595.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If I could just see the entire document in B/C/S, please, Your Honours. Thank you. That's accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now we're going to the lower left hand section of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you confirm there's no data in any of the --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- left hand section -- bottom left hand section of the document which we have been discussing with, I believe all of the documents before boxes 32, 37, 38, and 39.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that there's no information therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the -- below the documents -- below those boxes that we just referred, do you see any information whatsoever, handwritten or typewritten. Directly below those boxes, do you see anything at all in the document that you're looking at? Any handwriting like a note or anything else?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean below boxes 37, 38, and 39?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the copy before me, there is nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I would note for purposes of the record concerning the same document, in the English version it says "VSB," that's all in caps, "/expansion unknown/," then a line or two is dropped and it says "/handwritten:/Tomo Basevic." Tomo is spelled T-o-m-o, and Basevic is spelled B-a-s-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber would note that in the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- there is an abbreviation "VSB."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I just saw that abbreviation, Your Honour, and I -- therefore retract that particular remark, but with regard to the secondary remark concerning "/handwritten:/Tomo Basevic," I maintain the position that I previously took.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In respect of that document, sir, I wish to sight the original before I take a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And concerning the lower right-hand side of the document, can you confirm there is no stamp?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: P596, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now this document contains information contained in box 4; correct? On the upper left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, going to the bottom of the document - left-hand side - which would be on page 2 of the English, is there any information whatsoever in any of those boxes on the lower left-hand side concerning who it was approved by, from the sender's standpoint, who it was ordered by, from the sender's standpoint, who the manager was, from the sender's standpoint, or who it was entered by?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no information here whatsoever. But to avoid any confusion, the VSB acronym means the military printing office, Belgrade. That was the entity that produced this form. This was not a handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could turn to the right-hand side of this document, I note there is a stamp and signatures. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, using, for a moment, P596, for purposes of some of the discussion we've had before, and specifically referring to the bottom left-hand portion of this document, wherein there is no data whatsoever, could you tell us what, if any, problems or difficulties are created by this absence of information with regard to relying upon the accuracy of a delivery?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we talked about this yesterday, and we saw what the regulations were concerning this. In other words, without accurately entered information in the forms by the provider and without information confirming receipt, I cannot really take this to be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we now please see P597.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, I think we have before us a different kind of document, refreshingly. And I'd like you to take a look at the document and see whether you can be of any assistance and comment on what kind of a document is this?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the left-hand corner, information is missing about the sender. If I may put it that way. It says SOUR and then below that, RO, and then it says KR, in parentheses, and then it says telegram and telex. As far as can I see the number is 10 through 21. So a portion of the text is missing. Now, this is a form --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me stop you there for the moment. Do you know what SOUR stands for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an acronym for complex organisation of associated labour, because, at the time, that is what -- how business was done in our parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "at that time that is how business was done in our parts," is the -- and I'll use the acronym here, was the SOUR a state company, a private company? Could you be of some assistance to us with regard to that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The SOURs and OURs were state-owned companies, or, rather, socially owned companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that they were socially owned companies just -- for purposes of clarity, were these socially owned companies both under the SFRY and under FRY so that after the breakup of the former Yugoslavia in and FRY there still existed socially owned companies?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the SFRY they did exist; whereas, in FRY the process of privatisation began, or, rather, the transfer of property and capital was done in a different manner. So that, at first, and I'm not sure whether even to this day some of these remnants still live on, because this is a process, an ongoing process, and privatisation is under way in our parts. How far it has gone, I don't know, because I haven't really been privy to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it was a socially owned company, who was it owned by?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you're asking me about things that I'm not really an expert for. But I can say this. There used to exist state capital and social capital in our country and that is how the companies were also established and -- but I can't really tell you anything more about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this SOUR was this a company that was under the authority of the army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not within the army, but it was a state-owned company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the information that is contained in this document, looking at this information, can you tell us under the name of the item number 1, what is the item?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, under number 2, it says 82 millimetre shell M86.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What's that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I don't know, below that there is something reading 9301-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And in the box above that, number 1, what is -- what is inserted into that box?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it says there "incendiary shell, 120 millimetre."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now going to the right of -- of the number 1 where you think it says incendiary shell, 120 millimetre, there's a place that indicates how many were ordered and how many were issued. Can you confirm that that's what it says on the document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, under -- in the box entitled "Quantity," there are two sub-boxes. One of them reads "ord," "ord." I assume that that is the short form for "ordered." And then it says in the next box, "issued."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see the numbers are the same. So -- and I don't know if you can confirm this or not. I assume that what this means is that 20 incendiary grenades of the size 120 millimetres were ordered and the same was issued?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to -- with regard to the second box, which is referring to 82-millimetre grenades, M-86s, 100 were ordered and a hundred were issued.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. And we see a letter K before that, and I assume that stands for "pieces." So 100 were ordered and 100 were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the discussion that we were having the other -- we were having the other day, in terms of heavy weaponry, what is the significance, if any, of 120 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a shell that is used for mortars which has a 120-millimetre diameter or phi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And for the purposes of dealing with the issue of whether such a shell is a light weapon, a medium weapon, or a heavy weapon, are you in a position to give us any assistance in that regard as to whether or not a 120-millimetre shell could be designated in any of those three respects?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I said yesterday or the day before yesterday that under the Vienna Agreement, when the weapons for our army were supposed to be reduced, it was considered that all the weapons that were 76 millimetre in calibre were offensive weapons, but depending on the type of weapons, this would not -- could not be considered heavy weapons, because these weapons were part of infantry units. And I assume, as a technical person, that these weapons could not be considered to be of a heavy calibres because their range was not very large -- very long. That's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kodzopeljic, so that we can release you early for you to go home, can I request that you try to keep your answers as short as possible. When the question says "was this a light, medium, or heavy calibre weapon," just say light weapon or just say heavy, whichever the answer is. That will help us to move a little faster. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Once again, turning your attention to this document, do you see anywhere in the document the designation "to the purchaser." Are those words contained on the document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Once again, for purposes of record, they are contained in the English version directly under --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note they are contained in the B/C/S version as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Ah-hah. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the box right of the title, dispatch note number 115. It says Kupcu, K-u-p-c-u, and then there is handwritten 93.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at the very bottom of the document and there's a stamp there. Do you know who that stamp belonged to or what -- what that stamp signifies? And by "belong to," who is the company or the military unit or -- I think we've seen, for example, military units. Is that a military unit stamp?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What kind of a stamp is it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a stamp, a company stamp, the Krusik Corporation, from Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So with the information -- with the information that is supplied in the document to the purchaser, can you tell us, looking at this document, who the purchaser is?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that it is the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the basis of that assumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says: Dispatched to company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where does it say that, dispatched to the company. Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's below that, where it says in bold [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... under 115. It says dispatched to the company [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, finally, with regard to this document, do you see a date on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what date is that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: November 4, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could see plaintiff's 598.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The last dispatch note number we looked at in people's 597 was dispatch number 115. Could you tell us what the dispatch note number is on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you give us the date of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it's the 20th or 28th of December, and I assume 1993. 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say you assume 1993, do you see those numbers on this document a 9 and a 3.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 3 is legible but the 9, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. The last document that we looked at, P597, was dispatched to the company Drina Corps Vlasenica. Could you tell us, according to this document, who were the items dispatched to with regard to dispatch note number 175?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean what is -- what it says there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under number 1, incendiary shell, 120 -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All I'm asking is who was it dispatched to. It says, similar to the last document there's a notation of who this material is dispatched to. It says: Dispatched to the company. And who is the company that this is dispatched to?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military Post 7111, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if you look at the -- at the bottom, is it -- is this, once again, the Krusik stamp?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, you can see it at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm hoping can you help us here. Looking at these last two documents, considering the information that's contained in them with regard to the -- with -- a dispatch note number indicating to the purchaser and that the parties involved being the Drina Corps in the first document that we saw, 597, and VP Military Post 711, Vlasenica, in the second document. Could you tell us whether or not this involves the sale of these items, that these items were being sold that were being delivered?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it says that it has only been delivered.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the information considering it says to the purchasers. Is that of any help to us in that regard or not, or would you need further information to make that determination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: I have a question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, following this there should be an invoice sent to the company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this corporation the manufacturer, Krusik, Valjevo, was under the supervision or the control of the VJ according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it was not. It was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DAVID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated that there should be an invoice sent to the company. In the absence of the invoice, all you can tell us with regard to this document is that it is a -- it indicates that it was sent. I want to use your words directly. Yeah, there should be an invoice sent to the company. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the invoice may have sent by mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It may have been, but since we don't have one before us, I'm not asking you to speculate in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I figured out a way of speeding some of this up, so if you give me just a moment, I'm going to get through a series of these exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a company or institution called Pretis?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where was Pretis located?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, in 1993 was Pretis under the control of the Bosnia-Herzegovina government, the Republika Srpska government, or some other government?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was under the control of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, what was the function of Pretis?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really answer that with certainty, but some weapons systems, for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "some weapons systems for sure," were those weapons systems that were being produced? Were those weapons systems that were being repaired? Were those weapons systems that were being maintained? Any of those; all of those; none of those.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They actually manufactured weapons systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When -- when -- I just want to make sure that I'm understanding what you're saying with regard to the translations. Did you say weapons systems, did you say weaponry, or did you say weapons with regard to what Pretis manufactured.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said -- I said weapon assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "weapon assets," could you define for us what you mean by weapon assets.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance, a cannon. That is a weapon asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now with regard to the size of Pretis, if you know, and by that I mean physically, the size of the plant, can you tell us how big it was? If you know.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a big plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Do you by any chance -- once again if you know, if you don't know, that's fine. Do you by any chance have any idea as to what its production capacity was?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it was a big plant, can -- can you tell us once again if you know, from a standpoint of size, how many hectares or kilometres if it actually covered that kind of an area, it covered? And I do believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that, especially, I wouldn't know anything about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And just to remind the Chamber, I believe Pretis is one of the places that we had occasion to visit during our site visit. I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that if we are talking in terms of area, then kilometre would be an inappropriate word to use. It would have to be square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... you said hectares.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I said hectares and I should have said square kilometres. Could we please have P978.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at the upper left-hand corner. We still don't have the English up but that's where I will be focussing your attention. Whose the document from?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, logistics sector, technical department.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What is the date?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 28 June 1990 -- and I can't see what year exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Going down after the section that discusses who this is to be delivered to and where it says "for," there's a paragraph that says: "Based on the order of the head of staff, hd Pretis, from Vogosca shall issue the following ammunition types and quantities for the needs of the Ilidza pbr." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thereafter, there are six entries concerning various types of weapons or material for weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is ammunition. Shells, rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. That's perfect. That's fine. No need to go further, that's fine. And with regard to the bottom, it says that: "The approved ammunition shall be collected by an Ilidza Brigade representative. And the commands of the Ilidza Brigade and Vogosca headquarters, Pretis shall agree on the dynamics of delivery." Could you comment on that what means as to who was delivering what to who?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The holding corporation, Pretis, delivered assets to the Drina Brigade. They delivered the assets specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have P1064 on the screen. I'm sorry, I'm hearing a question. I'm not sure. I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, you you're saying the holding company or corporation Pretis delivered assets. I thought this would be an order, not a delivery. "Based on the order of the head of staff, hd Pretis from Vogosca shall issue the following." Is this something that is still to be issued? It's not been delivered yet. Whether it was delivered, there would have to be some other documentation following this one. That's my understanding. Wouldn't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are correct. I may have been wrong about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you so much. That's all [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just following up on your question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: All said and done, this is a transaction that exists between the VRS and Pretis. Those are the parties to this transaction?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for asking that question. When I hesitated, that's the question I wanted to ask. But can I follow up on it. Do you know what the command of Ilidza pbr Infantry Brigade is? You don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do know who the commander of the SRK, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then if you don't know the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I believe you wouldn't know the SRK, IKM-2, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps forward command post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know what "hd" stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Holding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 1064, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could take a moment and take a look at this document. There are a number -- there are a number of pages in the document, so I'd like you to take a look. Go to your binder, please, 1064. I think it might be easier for you, because that way you can look at all of the pages that are contained in this document. There's seven total pages in -- in hard copy in English.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If you could just -- if you could look at the document, just for a moment. Review the document. Have you had a chance to review the entire document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to the second page of the document, if I could. I believe that would be in -- in both English and in B/C/S. Looking at the very top of the page, where it says in B/C/S "ugovor." Could you identify for us what kind of a document this is?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a contract between two parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you look and tell us who the two parties are that this is a contract between?
