utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Unis Pretis of Vogosca, and Krusik of Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us what this subject matter is of the contract which is contained in Article 1?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1, primer to gun cartridge, and 3, primary charge for a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, below that could you tell us what it says with regard to this contract and equipment that this contract concerns is. There's a particular sentence right after the three items that you mentioned starting with "asortiman sredstava"? I'm getting better, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my document it says prices do not include packaging material because the purchaser is under an obligation to have it returned, if we're reading the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like you to -- we are reading the same document, but you've jumped ahead. I'm still in Article number 1. Right before we get to Article number 2. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I found it now. It says the contract can be amended by adding other types of products, as needed by the purchasing party.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who was the purchasing party?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: HK Krusik -- sorry. The purchasing party was Unis Pretis of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And who was the selling party?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The selling party was HK Krusik of Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd now like to go to Article 3. And in Article 3 -- which I think will be on the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I think you are going to have to just scroll down a bit in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In the B/C/S, the very last sentence on the page, could you tell us what the value of the contract between the buyer, Pretis, and the seller, Krusik, contemplated?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, could you go to the next page in B/C/S. And with regard to -- with regard to that, can you tell us what the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You have to scroll up to the top of the page. And you're going to have to scroll down in the English; I'm terribly sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us what obligation the buyer had to the seller with regards to payment?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buyer undertakes to pay, within a period of eight days from the date of the signing of the contract, an advance of 383.376 dinars, which amounts to 30 per cent of the total value of the contract, on the basis of an issued pro forma invoice to Giro account number 43900-601-7-2255 SDK, Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if we could now go to Article number 9 which will be -- perfect. That's going on to be page, I believe it's going to be on page 6 of the English. With regard to Article number 9 in terms of what occurs if there is a dispute, looking at the second paragraph, what do the contracting parties here contemplate with regard to the jurisdiction that will resolve any disputes that exists between them?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The competent court would be the district commercial court in Valjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to that -- that competent court, what do the contracting parties agree to with regard to whatever decision is reached in the event there is a dispute?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose decision is final and enforceable for both contracting parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And looking at the very bottom of the document do you -- do you see a stamp and a signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it. I see the stamps of both buyer and seller.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we leave this on the screen, because I'll have one or two questions. We'll take the break and come back at a quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that we left off with you indicating that you wanted the document left up on the screen because you had a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. It may just be one. Okay. Let me ask that question, and then I'll come back to what I wanted to say. Just for the record, are you able to read for us the stamps and names of the people at the bottom of that contract?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm receiving French, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Shall I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My apologies. Are you able to read for us the stamps and the names of the peoples who have signed the document at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The right-hand side of the document where it says buyer, it says "Unis Pretis, Vogosca." And on the stamp, I can read "Pretis, Vogosca, Unis, Pretis," and I can't make out the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The left-hand side stamp, or, actually, what I can read is as follows: "Seller, HK Krusik, DD," which means shareholding, "Valjevo." On the stamp I see that it says, "Krusik Holding Corporation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour, just before I start we seem to still be having technical problems. At this point Mr. Zorko, who also is our Case Manager, is not able to get on to any of the electric or electronic systems that we have, be they an S-system or any other kind of system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. While he is trying that, can I say what I want to say, which we can deal with without any electronics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I also -- sure, I had a second matter that I wanted to speak to briefly, but so be it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you need electronics to do what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, during the last break I took a look at what I had left to do. I also appreciate the amount of time we estimated for this witness, and I'm aware of the fact that I have exceeded that time, but I think that we'll be okay in terms of the overall amount of time that we have, and I have truncated my examination even more so so that I believe there will be but a few questions more of this witness. And then I will have concluded so that -- to the extent we made an estimate that was lesser than we thought, such things do occur in the fullness of a trial, but I think that with regard to ultimately amount of time that we'll be using we will be okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now when you say "but a few questions," how much longer do you think you're going to be? Because that's the point I wanted to raise with you anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sure. I think I will be no more than another 20 minutes, if that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead then [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to try to do this in the absence of Mr. Zorko's assistance. Hopefully it will work. If we could have up on the screen plaintiff's 1262. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you briefly take a look at this document and tell us, if you know, what kind of a document it is.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an order by the commander of Military Post 2082, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue that we have been discussing for these past days, armed with this order and nothing more, and by that I mean any of the material lists that we have been discussing, are you able to tell us whether or not this order was enacted or not; whether or not the materials contained in the order were delivered or left any depot or institution or not; whether they were received or not?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that this materiel was actually dispatched or sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said also that this is an order. Is this an order? Or is this a request based on an order? And I called it a request because it says: Please issue from the below-stated VPs. But based on an order number so-and-so, of so-and-so. The request is based on an order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In my version, it says: Issue for the needs of the General Staff. It's in the imperative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And briefly, looking at the kinds of materiel to be issued, under number 3, it has a number of rounds for 7.62-millimetre Browning. And is that number in terms of -- in terms of a military distribution is that a large number, a small number? It says 1.5 million pieces. Is that a normal distribution amount?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my book, this is a large quantity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Are you armed with any information as to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of refitting of ammunition, what period of time it would take to refit one and a half million rounds of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said already that the 7.62-millimetre calibre ammunition is not something that can be refitted. Hence, I can't say what the time amount would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to refitting ammunition, could you tell us with regard to -- in a generic sense the refitting of ammunition how long it would take to refit 1.5 million rounds of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honours. But if could I just have a moment to read the transcript. The witness has already answered that it can't be refitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He says 7.62-millimetre calibres cannot be refitted. The next question is with regards to refitting ammunition, could you tell us with regard to or in a generic sense. You stand by your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I change my objection to one of relevance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to 20-millimetre rounds, is that a round that can be refitted?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are asked to repeat the answer, Mr. Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Such rounds go through the process of general overhaul.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could you tell us approximately how long it would take to refit 20.000 rounds?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. It's done in batches and per work posts or places. The whole assembly line is 150 to 200 metres long. There are points and cubicles equipped in such a way so as to avoid any possibility of an explosion, hence, I truly can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, finally, with regard to the issue of -- of ammunition, could you tell us, if you know, what period of time it would take for the special-purpose industry factories that you are familiar with to produce 1.5 million rounds of ammunition, such as a 7.62-millimetre Browning.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The factory at Prvi Partizan produced 100 million rounds per year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. I understood. I think that we can do the math from that position. If we could -- if we could now have up on the screen 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, are you able to help us determine by looking at this document to whom it was addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is addressed to three military posts, Military Post 8800, Kragujevac; Military Post 5292, Novi Sad; and Military Post 5292, Bogutovacka Banja. That's what's stated at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Military Post 8080, Kragujevac; Military Post 4100, Novi Sad; and Military Post 9008, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could if we could turn our attention to 65 ter 838D.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the second paragraph in this document after you've had a chance to review the document.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to what is stated in the second paragraph of this document, is the issue of where and how requests were sent something that was a topic of the conversation that you were made aware of?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to what's said here: "In future please send your requests through the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army and the FRY Federal Ministry of Defence." Are you in a position to comment? If you are, that's fine; if you're not, that's fine as well. Are you in a position to comment as to why such an admonition would have been made to the Ministry of Interior of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that -- that was what was ordered. It was ordered for these things to be done in that manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I seek the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you standing up, Mr. Thomas, or are you just stretching.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm thinking, Your Honour, but I don't object to the admission of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D392, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, finally, if we could have 65 ter 647D pulled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us the date of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12 September 1990 -- I cannot make out the next digit. Still the same; I can't really make it out, although you have zoomed in on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go down to the second full paragraph where -- which starts off with some numbers. Could you read those numbers for us and see if that gives you any assistance with regard to dates as they relate to this document. They're the numbers 12.09.1993. And then there's some Cyrillic writing and then it says 0E08,00?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't find it in my version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. If you would go to your binder and go to the section which are Defence exhibits. Past the green -- past the green separator. There's a green separator. No, keep on going. There's a green separator in your binder. The other way. Yes. Keep on -- perfect. Looking for the number 647. Take a look at 647. Yes. And if you could --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Great. And if you could do us the kindness in the hard copy of looking at the first full paragraph after it says: "Note: From a meeting of the chief of the Yugoslav Army General Staff with responsible chiefs of General Staff administration following aggression by the Croatian army against the RSK/Republic of Serb Krajina/." The next paragraph. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see some numbers there?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to -- once again all I'm talking about is the date. I hope that will be become of some assistance to you with regard to this document. There was a meeting and looking at the list of attendees at this meeting, if you would go down to the fourth name from the very bottom of all the attendees. I'd ask if you take a look at that name and see if you recognise that name as being yours?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my name and last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to what occurred at that meeting, if you take a look at the second full paragraph after the list of names, could you tell us what that says.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "After brief consultations with the people responsible for NVO, which means weapons and materiel in the infantry, mechanised units, artillery, and other participants, he decided that requests by the Main Staff of the RSK for NVO and medical supplies should be met or approved only to the extent to which they do not deplete the current reserves of the Army of Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the last part of what you have told us: Only to the extent to which they do not deplete the current reserves of the Army of Yugoslavia, could you tell us why that was of importance?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the General Staff ordered that the needs of the Yugoslav Army should be regulated in this manner. So whatever does not affect that -- is not detrimental to the combat readiness of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to the issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to have to interrupt here because it is related to this very point. Now, the English translation of this document does not use the word "deplete," and I do know that the interpretation said "deplete." It says "endanger," and there is an substantive difference between the use of those two. Deplete means then you're left with nothing. Endanger means you are getting me to a stage where my combat readiness is now being threatened. So given those stages, you would stop supply earlier or sooner, if as soon as my supplies are endangered I would stop giving you a supply; but deplete means I'll give you everything that I have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will only read the next paragraph in that order.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters do not see the bottom of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters do not see the bottom of the English translation. Could we please lift it up. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness please read a bit more slowly, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please don't bring it down again. Now you're bringing down the bottom part of the English page. You may read now, Mr. Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it says the chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army has prohibited the deliveries of weapons and materiel to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Serbian Krajina which would endanger the norms that should be within the troop reserves of units and the critical assets at the level of the army.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: That paragraph is on the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we go to the next page in the English version so that Judge Moloto is able to see that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Guy-Smith, we are long ready. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Oh. Just wanted to make sure that you had an opportunity to see the information. I would move for the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D393, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I use the word "finally," I intend to maintain that position, but if I could have but a brief moment for conversation with my colleagues just to make sure that the "finally" is finally. I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kodzopeljic, for your time and your patience. My colleague on the other side of the room, I believe, may have a question or three to ask you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If I could just have a moment to organise myself with the lectern, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, you may have the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Kodzopeljic, good afternoon. My name is Barney Thomas. I'm a lawyer with the Prosecution. I have the opportunity now, sir, to ask you some questions about the testimony you have given over the last few days. I ask you, please, to listen carefully to the questions that I ask. Answer only the question that have I asked, and if you need any further clarification from me regarding any of my questions, please let me know. Is that clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I want to go back just to the first page of the document that we see on the screen, please. Now we see that that is dated September 1993. And we see from the list of names that you, at that time, occupied the position of the deputy chief of the technical administration; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, that document can come off the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The technical administration is part of the logistics sector of the General Staff of the VJ; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You went from the deputy chief of the technical administration to the chief of the technical administration.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not quite accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you stay as -- did you stay in the technical administration throughout the period of the war in Bosnia, in 1993 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: At any point during that period did you become the head of the technical administration?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The technical administration was, as I've already said, part of the logistics sector of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: As chief of that administration, you would have been subordinated to General Milovanovic who was the head of the logistics sector; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was the assistant chief of the General Staff for logistics, and I was his subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. His immediate superior was General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So you spent the entire period of 1993 to 1995 in the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You remained in the General Staff of the VJ until 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what is the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that for certain. I can't really be precise. Because, for me, of the chief of the technical administration, I had no ties to that administration. I had no orders or did I have -- nor did I have any need to have any kind of cooperation with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, sir, tell us what you know.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this was an institution that was established in Belgrade in order to enhance the cooperation between the Yugoslav Army and the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And how did it do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No idea?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was irrelevant for my work, for my job.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were six years in the General Staff and you don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just repeat that I had no common tasks with them that we should resolve together.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, we have looked at a number of material lists over the last three day, haven't we? A number of those refer to purported deliveries to the 30th Personnel Centre. As someone involved in logistics for six years as part of the General Staff of the VJ, can you please explain to us, in the context of deliveries of weapons and ammunition to the 30th Personnel Centre, what that means?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please kindly speak into his microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know in what sense you mean that, in what sense you want me to be more precise in my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just in case you haven't do so yet, there is a request from the interpreters that you try to speak closely to your microphone. I guess they find it a little hard to hear you, Mr. Kodzopeljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On delivery slips that we have seen, sir, the 30th Personnel Centre is named as the recipient, or intended recipient, of weapons and ammunition. Why, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us why the chief of the technical administration of the logistics sector of the VJ General Staff doesn't know the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, we took care of the quantities that we had in our warehouses, and we issued them as we received orders from our superiors so that we did not keep track. No documents were sent through the technical department. They were sent from the logistics basis, the 8th logistics basis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure that the number is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I follow you, sir. Can you please explain why you, holding the position that you did, cannot give us the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, any order that was sent relating to supplies that was sent from the chief of the General Staff would go to either the 6th logistics base or through the army command. It will not go through the technical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That doesn't explain, sir, why you, holding the position that you did in the General Staff from 1993 to 1999 does not know what that reference to the 30th Personnel Centre means. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: At this point I must rise, since the question has now been asked on a number of occasions. He has received an answer on a number of occasions. It may not be the answer that he wishes, but, nonetheless the question has been asked and answered now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Knowing, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, Mr. Thomas, there is an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I withdraw the question. Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, knowing, sir, what you know today, do you still not know the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say with full responsibility that only yesterday I read in a book some details about that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You discovered yesterday for the first time, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how you understood what I said. I told you that I read some details yesterday, and I've already said that I knew certain things which were of general nature that I was aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit P1009 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised that e-court is not responding. But I guess that's -- they're still trying to do their best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Looks like it's going to need a technician, Mr. Thomas, to be called in. If you are able to go to something else that doesn't need a document on the screen while we're waiting for the technician, it might be of help. If it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Let me just check for a moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see something on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Ah, thank you, Your Honour. And I want page 3 in the B/C/S, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Please take a moment to read that document, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What position did you hold in 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the chief of the technical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What does that document mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order by the president of the FRY on supplying the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with weapons and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And when the president of the federal republic orders the supply of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with weapons and military equipment, presumably the logistics sector of the VJ General Staff would have been aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You said that correctly. It was the logistics, or the rear sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So can you please tell me what supplying the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres with weapons and military equipment means?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I see this order for the first time. It is strictly confidential, and they are recorded separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It suggests, does it not -- well, it expressly states, does it not, that the chief of the General Staff is responsible for putting this into effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, that is pushing it a bit. It says that he's authorised. It doesn't say responsible. One being authorised one being responsible are distinct. At least in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, let's take -- I can rephrase the question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We can see that, as at 1994, there was an order from the president of the federal republic to supply arms to the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And military equipment too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The chief of the General Staff was authorised to reconcile the requests of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with the means of the army to deliver on those requests, wasn't he, by that order?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The logistics sector is immediately subordinated to the chief of the General Staff of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You were the technical -- you were the chief of the technical administration at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: How do you not know what this document means?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Has he said so? Did he say he doesn't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He says he hasn't seen it, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, those are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. One is he hasn't seen it, but now that he's seeing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. But then you're saying how do you say -- how can you say -- how do you not know what this document means? What I'm asking you is, has he said he doesn't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He says he hasn't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. That's a different story.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But does that mean he doesn't know what means?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm asking him, sir. Reading it now for the first time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but the question is -- there is no connection between the two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What was the logistics sector responsible for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In a general sense.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rear, or logistics sector, was in charge of providing technical support, medical support, quartermaster supplies, veterinary support, and construction support.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And support to whom?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And we see from this document that includes the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We can take that off the screen. Can we have document P575 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now you may recall, sir, that when you looked at this document yesterday you were asked about whether the handwriting at the very top next to the number 044, either 6 or 8 or 0, at 0641, was the word "Tisca," and you told us that you couldn't see any writing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I have the original of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm -- I assume that Mr. Thomas intends on showing the witness the document, and I certainly have no trouble in that regard. I should also inform the Court that I have seen the document. Mr. Thomas was kind enough to show me the document prior to the proceedings today and, having seen the original of the document, as he confirmed previously with regard to documents in which insertions were made in the English that did not exist, I can tell that you I have seen the original and the word handwritten "Tisca" does appear to the satisfaction of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that indication, Your Honours. I need not deal with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But before do you that, just so that the Chamber is with the both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What are we talking about? Unfortunately, I've been trying to get this exhibit on my -- the screen that can I control, so I can enlarge it enough for me to see. This size can't I read. Where is this Tisca now again?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If Your Honour looks at the right-hand side, right at the very top right-hand corner of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Top. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There is handwritten entered "Tisca."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On the B/C/S which -- yeah. Handwritten, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And there was dispute yesterday as to whether or not it appeared on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I understand is that Mr. Thomas went back and obtained the original from the archives. It was a matter that I think you at some discussed with regard -- no, I don't know if it was specifically for this document or other documents. I had an opportunity to look at the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- with Mr. Thomas, and as I said, the Defence agrees that that handwritten word is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Yes, Mr. Thomas, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. There is one other, sir, that I'd like to just clarify. If we can have P581 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith is on his feet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to this document, if I'm not mistaken, there had been an examination as to whether or not there was or was not a signature in box number 36. I've had an opportunity once again to review the original, it was taken from the archives, and having examined the original as taken from the archives, I would concur with what I believe is my colleague's position, that there is in fact a signature that can be seen on the original document which is not to be found on the copy that we have been reviewing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- may I suggest that if there are any other documents that the two of you have discussed and over which you have come to an agreement, can we just list them for the record and skip them if you are agreed and forget asking the witness about it so that we can move on to some other issues that are contentious.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There are none, sir. There are just those two. Can we have document P573 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sir, while this document is coming up on the screen, you were taken to a number of material lists over the last few days where you were asked to comment on the absence of materiel -- no, the absence of appropriate entries being made in the document and in particularly in relation to box 4, where the name and address of sender would not be recorded. You see that this is one of those documents. The question I have for you though, sir, is that there are, despite the absence of any entries in box number 4, there are other indicators on that document of who the sender of materiel was, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would have to for the first time make an objection that I don't think I've made here, which is argumentative by virtue of the use of the term "despite." That that would qualify the question asked as being argumentative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm not going to waste time, Your Honour. I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: One way to tell who sent materiel was to look at box 4, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Another way to determine who sent materiel is to look at other boxes in the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Without that particular box, you cannot see who sent it. It identifies the sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Look at box number 3 -- sorry. Look at box number 2, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ...zoom in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you see an entry for the military post of the sender?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It says military post, MFO, or financial organ, of the fourth level or degree, which needn't necessarily be the sender.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You see the place of the sender in box number 11?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We see also the box above that which shows the military bookkeeping centre of this particular sender, don't we?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just for our own assistance, sir, where are Paracin and Nis?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paracin is to the north of Nis. Nis is to the south of Paracin. We can say that Nis is in the south of Serbia and Paracin in central Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, that's my question. Thank you. If we scroll to the right-hand side of the document, a name has just caught my eye. We see there the recipient being the Drina Corps Command and the destination station of the receiver being Tisca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Destination station Tisca, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go down to the bottom right-hand corner of the document, sir. We have seen many of these, namely a signature and a stamp of the receiver, and, presumably, the regulations require these to be placed on the document once delivery has been received.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can take that document off the screen. And can we please have document -- Exhibit P576 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were also asked about a number of entries where the sender was shown as being the General Staff of the VJ, and a number of those entries had a name in brackets afterwards. For example, this document, "Bog. Banja." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we look at the first line of what is supplied, it appears to be something in relation to a shape -- something in relation to a self-propelled M-18 gun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It says round, 76 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: For what, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a self-propelled piece called M-18.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is there a military post called Bogutovacka Banja?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There is no VJ Military Post in Bogutovacka Banja?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Where is Bogutovacka Banja?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In central Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go to document P1269, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just before we do that. Can we get some clarification with regard to the English translation of "self-propelled gun."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would Mr. Guy-Smith please move a little closer to his microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, I do apologise. Could we get some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] Put it a little closer, put it a little closer. That's better.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we get some clarification with regard to the translation here of "self-propelled gun." It now says "self-propelled piece," and I don't know which particular translation we're dealing with. A gun is certainly distinct for a piece and to the extent that these documents have exhibited difficulties with the information contained therein and to the extent that the Chamber is going to be relying on these documents for whatever purpose, ultimately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where does it say piece?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The witness said piece. The document in English says gun. It says "/self-propelled gun/," and there seems to be a distinction here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't then we -- I guess we rather know what a self-propelled gun is. Shouldn't we get a translation of what the witness meant by piece?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour. It's just before we leave the document, I think we have some clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And can the witness also confirm that he said "piece" and not "gun."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: He said self-propelled piece on line 7 -- at page 71, line 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. What do you mean by self-propelled piece, Mr. Kodzopeljic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A self-propelled piece. M-18 is an asset with a mounted gun. It's a 30-ton piece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I also heard you say what is ordered here are rounds, not -- what -- I mustn't put words into your mouth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't make this out precisely but it says "Metak," I think. Metak, 76 millimetres, meaning round.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we have P1269 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You will see, sir, that this is a document dated 19 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we please go to the second page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You can see from the document, sir, that it is issued by one Lieutenant-Colonel Jevrem Cokic. Do you know what position he held at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's Lieutenant-General Jevrem Cokic, 1st Army Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: He is commander of the 1st Army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page in the English, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you look, please, General -- sorry, Mr. Kodzopeljic, at the first paragraph of the document, I want to ask you, first of all, the same question that His Honour Judge Moloto asked you. There's a reference to an order issued by the chief of the General Staff of the VJ, and what we have in the English translation is: "Please issue from the below-stated VPs, military posts, the following types and quantities of ammunition for the needs of the General Staff of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska." And my question, sir, is: Is it correct that the term there is "please issue," or is it the imperative version, as you stated before?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the imperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please scroll down to point number 4 in the English. Now, that is an instruction to a Military Post number 5292-1 in Bogutovacka Banja to issue rounds for a self-propelled -- 76-millimetre rounds for a self-propelled M-18 weapon, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for that self-propelled weapon or piece, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could we please look at document P575.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now we have the sender's details in box number 4 being, again, defective in your view. We have military post -- I'm sorry, we have an entry 5, question mark 92, Mrsac Kraljevo. Was there a VJ Military Post number 5292 in Mrsac?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain. Although I suppose as much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, if there -- okay. We will see there that the second entry of materiel includes 2.000 rifle grenades. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that written by hand in my version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can we go back to P1269, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, while the English is being blown up, look at point number 3, please.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You see a reference there to Military Post 5292, Mrsac. You see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: To supply 2.000 -- amongst other things 2.000 pieces -- 2.000 rifle grenades. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And this was the same document we were looking at a moment ago which is the order of the 1st Army commander based on the decision of General Perisic. And we will see that the date of that order --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we scroll to the top of the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: -- is 19 November 1993. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says contact-fuse rifle grenade. Not just rifle grenade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you agree, sir, that the date of the order is 19 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my document, it also says the 19th of November of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have one remaining delivery slip relevant to this document. I can deal with it very quickly and that will be the end of the delivery slips, if you will grant me the indulgence to just continue for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your opposite number is on his feet. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm just unclear about one thing because you say Mr. Thomas is referring to "an order" and he also used the term "decision," and in the English of P1269 the first paragraph discusses an order ST conference number 6748-2 of 12.11.1993 by commander of the GS VJ, General Staff of Yugoslavia, and another one, which is 6748-1 of 12.11.1993. And I'm unclear as to whether or not he is referring to that as being the order or the document itself that he is discussing with Mr. Kodzopeljic being the order. If we could just have some clarification, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I was referring to the order of the 1st Army commander, sir. So if we could go -- if I can be permitted to continue for just a few moments, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. The last document, please, P578.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you look in box number 4, sir, we have a reference to the sender being the Yugoslav Army General Staff Bogovada. Where is Bogovada, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my document it says VJ Bogovadza, and as I told you already it is in central Serbia. It's a warehouse. I can tell that you in that particular warehouse there was materiel stored originating or being assigned to a number of different military posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So do you now suggest, sir, that the reference in box number 4 is likely to that warehouse?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my presumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And maybe to add force to your presumption, if we look at the materiel supplied we have 7.9-millimetre rounds, 800.000 -- 800.100. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 800.100 pieces. However, this is only my presumption. It was entered by the handler or actually the person receiving it. It is the same handwriting. He presumed it had arrived from that particular warehouse in Serbia. He was probably told or learned by other means that this was so. However, I can't tell you with any precision that it was indeed sent by the military post in Bogovadza. I would need additional documents to corroborate, if this is actually true.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we go to P1269 for the last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought you said this was the last document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This was the last document to enable me to finish 1269, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: This is the same 1st Army document we were -- 1st Army order we were looking at before, sir, and you will see entry number 1, Military Post VP 8236, Bogovadza, 800.000 rounds of 7.9 ammunition. You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: One last question before we finish. Can you tell the name of the book, sir, that you were reading that was telling you all about the 30th Personnel Centre?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was written by Colonel Vuksic. I don't know the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Kodzopeljic, just to remind you once again that you are not supposed to discuss the case until you are excused from testifying. We stand adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 8th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
